Q: Desktop alerts say Antivirus disabled but the user never turned it off. What is likely?
Option1: Rogue or unwanted software tampering with security

Q: Files are renamed with .locked and cannot be opened. First response?
Option1: Disconnect from network and start incident response for ransomware

Q: Multiple personal files are missing after pop up infections. What is the best step?
Option1: Run full anti malware scan and restore from known good backup

Q: Unwanted notifications appear from the browser even when not on that site. Cause?
Option1: Push notifications allowed for a malicious site

Q: Windows Update fails with insufficient storage. What is the fix?
Random frequent pop ups in the browser. First step?
Option1: Check and remove malicious extensions and reset the browser

Q: When opening an HTTPS site you get a certificate name mismatch. Likely cause?
Option1: Man in the middle or captive portal

Q: Certificate warnings occur only on public Wi Fi. What is a safe step?
Option1: Open a non HTTPS site to trigger captive portal then connect securely

Q: Browser search redirects to unknown sites. What to inspect first?
Option1: Proxy settings and extensions then hosts file and DNS

Q: OS update fails with 0x8024xxx. BITS service is stopped. Most likely cause?
Option1: Malware tampering with update services and policies

Q: Unable to access network after VPN disconnect. ipconfig shows no default gateway. Fix?
Option1: Reset adapter or renew IP to restore default route

Q: False antivirus warnings ask for payment. What should you do first?
Option1: Terminate the process and run trusted anti malware tools

Q: Browser redirection persists after extension cleanup. Next best step?
Option1: Check hosts file and DNS resolver cache then run malware scan

Q: A user sees certificate warnings on the internal web app only. What is most likely?
Option1: Missing enterprise root CA in Trusted Root store

Q: Updates fail and error says not connected to update service. What first?
Option1: Check Windows Update service state and service dependencies

Q: Search queries redirect and a mysterious proxy appears in LAN settings. First remediation step?
Option1: Remove proxy in Internet Options and check for malicious extensions
